newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac to bid for Bank Melbourne -papers.
newsitem.headline: Westpac to bid for Bank Melbourne -papers.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp Ltd would announce later on Thursday it would make a takeover bid of between A$1.3 billion and A$1.5 billion for Bank of Melbourne Ltd, newspapers reported on Thursday.

"Parties close to the bid said Bank of Melbourne's board met yesterday to consider an offer pitched at A$8.80 (per share), with a special fully franked dividend of 90 cents per share," the Australian Financial Review reported.
"Allowing for the value of franking, that makes a total price of A$10.20 a share -- just under A$1.5 billion in total," the Financial Review said.
The Sydney Morning Herald said Westpac was expected to offer A$9.70 a share plus a special dividend, valuing Bank of Melbourne at A$1.3 billion or 2.6 times net tangible assets.
The Australian said Westpac would bid about A$10.00 per share plus a special dividend of about 50 cents a share, valuing Bank of Melbourne at A$1.39 billion.
Bank of Melbourne's share price jumped 65 cents to A$8.80 on Wednesday before the bank asked for a trading halt to be put on its shares.
The halt is scheduled to end at the beginning of trade on Thursday or when an announcement about a "confidential proposal" is made to the market, whichever is earlier.
Analysts said late on Wednesday there was speculation about a Westpac bid, but said the bank would have a tough time convincing regulators and the government to agree to such a merger.

Treasurer Peter Costello, who must approve any bank merger, said last week that he did not expect any merger applications while the goverment was still considering the findings of the official Wallis inquiry into the financial system.
Costello is due to release the Wallis report next week. The report is widely expected to recommend the relaxation of big bank merger rules.

But the anti-monopoly watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), has also said it would not allow a bank merger that left a state banking market without at least one substantial regional bank.
Bank of Melbourne is currently the only significant regional bank in Victoria.
The Sydney Morning Herald said Bank of Melbourne and Westpac approached ACCC chairman Allan Fels in late 1995 about a merger, but were told that it would not be passed.
Westpac's share price closed down 23.7 cents at A$6.873 on Wednesday, due largely to news that Lend Lease Corp had sold 15 million Westpac shares and fears it would sell more.
